name: Express Entry ranking changes effective 3 November 2026 (job offers and Canadian experience)
name_fr: Changements au système de classement de l'Entrée express au 3 novembre 2026
description: From 3 November 2026 Express Entry adds a 'labour market integration' factor that gives points for either Canadian work experience or a qualifying job offer (whichever is higher), rewards high-wage occupations, and no longer requires an LMIA for a job offer to count.

attributes.legal_status: announced; in force from 2026-11-03 (four days after the access date)
attributes.canadian_work_experience_points: work-length points unchanged (35–70 with spouse, 40–80 without, for 1 to 5+ years) plus high-wage bonus of 70 / 40 / 20 where the occupation's national median wage is at least 2.0x / 1.5x / 1.3x the average median wage, after at least 12 months (1,560 h) in high-wage occupations
attributes.job_offer_points: 100 / 70 / 50 for a qualifying offer in an occupation at 2.0x / 1.5x–2.0x / 1.3x–1.5x the average median wage; 0 below 1.3x
attributes.lmia: No longer required for a job offer to count for programme eligibility or CRS points; an LMIA adds no points; officers assess genuineness. The online profile still asks for a positive LMIA until updated (placeholder details on the IRCC page).
attributes.fsw_fst_job_offers: For programme eligibility, offers may be in any eligible TEER 0–3 job, not only high-wage occupations
attributes.transition: Profiles are recalculated on 3 November 2026 (up to two weeks); invitation rounds pause meanwhile. Candidates must update profiles before 3 November to receive job-offer points.
attributes.status_dependency: Matters only if the user has Canadian work experience or a Canadian job offer — both unknown (USER-PROFILE.md 'Work mode', 'Occupation').

sources.title: 2026 changes to points for Canadian work experience and job offers in the Express Entry system (modified 2026-10-16)
Canada refocusing Express Entry on top talent that drives economic growth (news release, October 2026; via search extract)

verification.notes: IRCC changes page fetched directly; the release was read through a search extract. Wording of wage thresholds differs slightly between the release ('median wage') and the changes page ('average median wage'); the changes page is used.

limitations: The list of occupations that qualify as high-wage was not captured. Re-check after 3 November 2026 that the change took effect as announced.
